observations: Torah #233 contains exactly two explicit bechina statements, both already captured in the dataset. No third cluster of 3+ concepts connected by bechina language exists anywhere in the source text. The Torah is structurally minimal: it presents a single good/evil mirror pair (Package 1 and Package 2) and then draws a practical conclusion from it (eitza). The practical teaching — that two thoughts cannot coexist, and therefore evil thoughts can be expelled by replacing them with something else — is framed entirely in causal and instructional language, not bechina language. The concepts mentioned in the practical section (Torah, prayer, business dealings, passive non-action) are examples of alternative thought-content, introduced as options for what to think about; none are equated to any other concept via bechina language. The general parent statement 'הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת הֵם בָּאִים מִבְּחִינַת הַחַיּוֹת' is a conceptual bridge linking the parable to the teaching, not a distinct third package. The dataset is complete for this Torah.
